claims.text: The desk turns Francesco Marconi's INMA deck, When journalism becomes intelligence, into seventeen pages on synthetic records.
claims.quote: turns Francesco Marconi's INMA deck, When journalism becomes intelligence, into seventeen pages on synthetic records

claims.text: A vault is a folder of files, encrypted, versioned like git and opened with a key; this one is published with its read key and opens as an app.
claims.quote: A vault is a folder of files, encrypted, versioned like git, and opened with a key.

claims.text: Every page has the same frame: the menu on the left in five groups, the page in the middle, and a details panel on the right that opens anything clicked with the record behind it.
claims.quote: Every page has the same frame.

claims.text: The cover says what is inside: 12 event families, 78 event types, an ontology, 16 records, 17 observations and a tracker.
claims.quote: 12 event families, 78 event types, an ontology, 16 records, 17 observations and a tracker

claims.text: The advantage page counts 13 registries and sources watched, 78 event types recognised, and seven observations compared with an earlier one, which is where the stories are.
claims.quote: seven observations that were compared with an earlier one, which is where the stories are

value.unit: observations compared with an earlier one

claims.text: Delta science is a before and after of the same landscape: not the landscape, but what changed in it, and the record that says so.
claims.quote: not the landscape, but what changed in it, and the record that says so

claims.text: Who wants what names the four actors of the deck's system map, the power provider, the developer, the local government and the residents, and who each is in Mesa Ranch.
claims.quote: names the four actors of the deck's system map and what each wants

claims.text: The deck shows 12 of the 78 event types; the vault has all 78, and most have not been seen yet, which is the point of an atlas.
claims.quote: The deck shows 12 of 78; the vault has all 78, and most have not been seen yet

value.unit: event types shown in the deck

claims.text: Every event type in the atlas has a definition and an observable signal.
claims.quote: each with a definition and an observable signal

claims.text: The domain ontology has six entities and six relationships, and the rule the vault follows is that an event changes a state or relationship in this model.
claims.quote: an event changes a state or relationship in this model

claims.text: Every observation has the deck's four folders, January to September 2026, and all seventeen observations with time, subject, change, event type and evidence, each stamped synthetic.
claims.quote: each with its time, subject, change, event type and evidence

claims.text: The AI workflow steps through one cycle, observe, compare, check, report and update: the first phase moved from the second half of 2027 to the first half of 2028.
claims.quote: in April the first phase was due in the second half of 2027; now it is the first half of 2028

claims.text: Journalists direct puts the deck's three verbs over three queues: what to monitor, what to investigate, what to publish.
claims.quote: what to monitor, what to investigate, what to publish

claims.text: The community tracker records 140 qualifying jobs in the school-district application against 120 in the state tax registration, and an open question about how many are local.
claims.quote: 140 qualifying jobs in the school-district application, 120 in the state tax registration

value.unit: qualifying jobs claimed in the school-district application

claims.text: The fractal semantic graph opens level by level from the question to actors and campus, families, event types, observations and records, the same shape at every level.
claims.quote: It is the same shape at every level, which is what makes a graph fractal.

claims.text: Drawn with every level at once, the rings show that most event types have no observation yet and a few branches carry all the news.
claims.quote: a few branches carry all the news

claims.text: The knowledge graph in time builds itself one observation at a time, and every relationship carries the observation that created it and, if one did, the one that ended it.
claims.quote: Every relationship carries the observation that created it and, if one did, the one that ended it.

claims.text: Records to observations draws the evidence between sixteen records and seventeen observations; the developer's April statement alone supports three.
claims.quote: the developer's April statement alone supports three

claims.text: The delta chain shows where the stories came from: every arc is a change that only a record of the earlier state could reveal.
claims.quote: every arc is a change that only a record of the earlier state could reveal

claims.text: To make a desk for your own patch, clone the vault with its read key, replace the families, entities, records and question, and run the three scripts; the editorial work is the part that matters.
claims.quote: The pages do not change. The editorial work is the part that matters

claims.text: The records are synthetic: every name and record in the vault is invented.
claims.quote: Every name and record in the vault is invented.

claims.text: The desk does not watch anything live; it runs the method on fixed records.
claims.quote: It runs the method on fixed records.

claims.text: The atlas beyond the slide is the newsroom's own; the deck shows 12 of its 78 event types.
claims.quote: The atlas beyond the slide is ours.

claims.text: It is not Marconi's work or endorsed by him; it is the newsroom's reading of his public slides.
claims.quote: It is our reading of his public slides.

claims.text: The article was requested on 15 October 2026 after seeing the vault; every screenshot is of the vault as published that day.
claims.quote: Every screenshot is of the vault as published on 15 October 2026
